root_cause.text: In nfc_unregister_device(), rfkill_unregister() was called while holding device_lock, creating a lock ordering inversion with rfkill_fop_write() which holds rfkill_global_mutex and then tries to acquire device_lock, resulting in a deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description details the deadlock scenario: Thread A (rfkill_fop_write) holds rfkill_global_mutex and waits for device_lock via nfc_rfkill_set_block->nfc_dev_down, while Thread B (nfc_unregister_device) holds device_lock and waits for rfkill_global_mutex via rfkill_unregister. The patch moves rfkill_unregister and rfkill_destroy outside the device_lock critical section.

The patch moves rfkill_unregister and rfkill_destroy outside the device_lock critical section.

    All NFC devices will now get proper RFKILL support as long as they provide

bic_trace_step.reason: In nfc_unregister_device, the commit adds device_lock(&dev->dev) before calling rfkill_unregister() and releases it after.
